paper.title: May 2023 Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL Paper 1 TZ1
paper.solution_status: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 5]

Point P has coordinates (−3, 2), and point Q has coordinates (15, −8). Point M is the midpoint of [PQ].

(a) Find the coordinates of M. [2]

Line L is perpendicular to [PQ] and passes through M.

(b) Find the gradient of L. [2]

(c) Hence, write down the equation of L. [1]
questions.summary: Find a midpoint and the equation of a perpendicular bisector.
questions.solution: (a) M = ((−3+15)/2, (2−8)/2) = (6, −3). (b) The gradient of PQ is −10/18 = −5/9, so the perpendicular gradient is 9/5. (c) Thus L is y + 3 = (9/5)(x − 6), equivalently y = (9/5)x − 69/5.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 7]

The function f is defined by f(x) = (7x + 7)/(2x − 4) for x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ 2.

(a) Find the zero of f(x). [2]

(b) For the graph of y = f(x), write down the equation of
    (i) the vertical asymptote;
    (ii) the horizontal asymptote. [2]

(c) Find f⁻¹(x), the inverse function of f(x). [3]
questions.summary: Find a rational function's zero, asymptotes and inverse.
questions.solution: (a) 7x+7=0 gives x=−1. (b)(i) The denominator vanishes at x=2. (ii) The ratio of leading coefficients gives y=7/2. (c) From y=(7x+7)/(2x−4), x=(4y+7)/(2y−7). Hence f⁻¹(x)=(4x+7)/(2x−7), x≠7/2.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]

On a Monday at an amusement park, a sample of 40 visitors was randomly selected as they were leaving the park. They were asked how many times that day they had been on a ride called The Dragon. This information is summarized in the following frequency table.

Number of times on The Dragon | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
Frequency                     | 6 | 16 | 13 | 2 | 3

It can be assumed that this sample is representative of all visitors to the park for the following day.

(a) For the following day, Tuesday, estimate
    (i) the probability that a randomly selected visitor will ride The Dragon;
    (ii) the expected number of times a visitor will ride The Dragon. [4]

It is known that 1000 visitors will attend the amusement park on Tuesday. The Dragon can carry a maximum of 10 people each time it runs.

(b) Estimate the minimum number of times The Dragon must run to satisfy demand. [2]
questions.summary: Use sample frequencies to estimate a probability, expectation and capacity.
questions.solution: (a)(i) 34 of 40 visitors rode, so the estimate is 34/40=0.85. (ii) E(X)=(16+2·13+3·2+4·3)/40=60/40=1.5 rides. (b) Estimated rides are 1000(1.5)=1500; at 10 riders per run, at least 150 runs are needed.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

(a) Show that the equation cos 2x = sin x can be written in the form 2sin²x + sin x − 1 = 0. [1]

(b) Hence, solve cos 2x = sin x, where −π ≤ x ≤ π. [5]
questions.summary: Convert a double-angle equation to a quadratic in sine and solve it.
questions.solution: (a) Since cos2x=1−2sin²x, equality gives 2sin²x+sin x−1=0. (b) Factor: (2sin x−1)(sin x+1)=0. Thus sin x=1/2 or −1. On the stated interval, x=π/6, 5π/6 or −π/2.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 6]

Find the range of possible values of k such that e^(2x) + ln k = 3e^x has at least one real solution.
questions.summary: Use a discriminant to find when an exponential equation has a real solution.
questions.solution: Let u=e^x>0. Then u²−3u+ln k=0. A real root requires 9−4ln k≥0, so k≤e^(9/4). Also ln k requires k>0. At equality u=3/2>0, and for every 0<k≤e^(9/4) at least one root is positive. Therefore 0<k≤e^(9/4).

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]

The function f is defined by f(x) = sin(qx), where q > 0. The following diagram shows part of the graph of f for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4m, where x is in radians. There are x-intercepts at x = 0, 2m and 4m.

[Graph: a sine curve of amplitude 1 starts at (0,0), has a maximum at (m,1), crosses at (2m,0), has a minimum at (3m,−1), and crosses again at (4m,0). Axes continue to 6m and from y=−4 to y=4.]

(a) Find an expression for m in terms of q. [2]

The function g is defined by g(x) = 3sin(2qx/3), for 0 ≤ x ≤ 6m.

(b) On the axes above, sketch the graph of g. [4]
questions.summary: Relate the period of a sine graph to a parameter and sketch a transformation.
questions.solution: (a) The period of f is 4m=2π/q, so m=π/(2q). (b) g has amplitude 3 and period 3π/q=6m. It starts at (0,0), reaches (3m/2,3), crosses at (3m,0), reaches (9m/2,−3), and ends at (6m,0), joined by a sinusoidal curve.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 13]

The function h is defined by h(x) = 2xe^x + 3, for x ∈ ℝ. The following diagram shows part of the graph of h, which has a local minimum at point A.

[Diagram: coordinate axes and the curve y=h(x), with its local minimum labelled A.]

(a) Find the value of the y-intercept. [2]

(b) Find h′(x). [2]

(c) Hence, find the coordinates of A. [5]

(d) (i) Show that h″(x) = (2x + 4)e^x.
    (ii) Find the values of x for which the graph of h is concave-up. [4]
questions.summary: Differentiate an exponential product to find a minimum and concavity interval.
questions.solution: (a) h(0)=3. (b) By the product rule, h′(x)=2e^x+2xe^x=2e^x(x+1). (c) Since e^x>0, h′=0 gives x=−1; h(−1)=3−2/e, so A=(−1,3−2/e). (d)(i) Differentiating gives h″=2e^x(x+1)+2e^x=(2x+4)e^x. (ii) As e^x>0, h″>0 exactly when 2x+4>0, so x>−2.

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 14]

Consider the arithmetic sequence u₁, u₂, u₃, …. The sum of the first n terms of this sequence is given by Sₙ = n² + 4n.

(a) (i) Find the sum of the first five terms.
    (ii) Given that S₆ = 60, find u₆. [4]

(b) Find u₁. [2]

(c) Hence or otherwise, write an expression for uₙ in terms of n. [3]

Consider a geometric sequence, vₙ, where v₂ = u₁ and v₄ = u₆.

(d) Find the possible values of the common ratio, r. [3]

(e) Given that v₉₉ < 0, find v₅. [2]
questions.summary: Derive arithmetic terms from partial sums and link them to a geometric sequence.
questions.solution: (a)(i) S₅=25+20=45. (ii) u₆=S₆−S₅=60−45=15. (b) u₁=S₁=5. (c) uₙ=Sₙ−Sₙ₋₁=n²+4n−[(n−1)²+4(n−1)]=2n+3. (d) v₄/v₂=r²=15/5=3, so r=±√3. (e) Since v₉₉=v₂r⁹⁷<0 while v₂=5, r=−√3. Thus v₅=v₂r³=5(−√3)³=−15√3.

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 17]

An object moves along a straight line. Its velocity, v m s⁻¹, at time t seconds is given by v(t) = −t³ + (7/2)t² − 2t + 6, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. The object first comes to rest at t = k.

[Graph: v starts positive at t=0, decreases to a local minimum, rises to a local maximum, then decreases through the t-axis at t=k and becomes negative.]

At t = 0, the object is at the origin.

(a) Find the displacement of the object from the origin at t = 1. [5]

(b) Find an expression for the acceleration of the object. [2]

(c) Hence, find the greatest speed reached by the object before it comes to rest. [5]

(d) Find the greatest speed reached by the object for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. [2]

(e) Write down an expression that represents the distance travelled by the object while its speed is increasing. Do not evaluate the expression. [3]
questions.summary: Use integration and differentiation to analyse displacement, acceleration and speed.
questions.solution: (a) Displacement is ∫₀¹v(t)dt=[−t⁴/4+7t³/6−t²+6t]₀¹=71/12 m. (b) a(t)=v′(t)=−3t²+7t−2. (c) a=0 gives (3t−1)(t−2)=0, so t=1/3 or 2. Before the first rest, the greatest velocity occurs at t=2 and v(2)=8; greatest speed is 8 m s⁻¹. (d) Also check t=4: v(4)=−10, so the greatest speed on [0,4] is 10 m s⁻¹. (e) Speed increases on [1/3,2] and [k,4], so one expression is ∫_(1/3)^2 v(t)dt − ∫_k^4 v(t)dt.
